name: Vanthorpe Meridian Blazer
description:
Vanthorpe's answer to the question of what a corporate professional wears when the meeting isn't formal enough for a suit but casual isn't acceptable. The Meridian Blazer is a single-breasted two-button in a medium-weight wool-poly blend available in charcoal, navy, and a dark forest that reads almost black in poor light. The construction is half-canvassed — more structure than a dress blazer, less than a suit jacket — and the lapels are a modest notch cut that doesn't date quickly. Interior pockets are deep and numerous, a Vanthorpe signature. The lining is a deep burgundy silk-analog that shows only when the jacket opens.

This is the jacket that Tier 3 professionals live in. It goes over a dress shirt for a client meeting and over a henley for a working lunch. It's been carefully designed to communicate that the wearer is serious without being ostentatious, which is exactly the register that Tier 3 corporate culture requires. Tier 4 buyers occasionally pick it up as a casual alternative to their bespoke pieces. It is not an exciting jacket. It is a jacket that works every day for years.
what_it_says: You're competent, reliable, and you understand what the room expects of you.
worn_by: people interviewing for the next tier
story_hooks: A blazer left in a conference room after a late meeting contains a folded note in the interior pocket — handwritten, in a cipher, addressed to no one.
Someone has been attending Tier 4 corporate events in a Meridian Blazer, passing as an analyst; they've been doing it for months and nobody has caught them.
The burgundy lining of a specific production batch was dyed with a compound that reacts faintly to a particular scanner frequency — nobody at Vanthorpe will say why.

physical_description.visual_profile: A refined single-breasted blazer with restrained elegance; creates a sharp, professional silhouette without aggressive tailoring. Medium length hits at the hip. Notch lapels sit close to the body with subtle definition. Projects authority without flash—the uniform of mid-tier corpo climbers and established working professionals.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive; designed for layering and movement. Shoulders are structured but not exaggerated. Sleeves taper gently to the wrist. Slight suppression at the waist suggests intentional design without embracing the body. Accommodates dress shirts and casual henley base layers with equal ease.
physical_description.primary_material: Medium-weight wool-poly blend (likely 65% wool, 35% synthetic for durability and crease recovery). Half-canvassed construction provides internal structure without rigidity.
physical_description.texture: Subtle surface sheen characteristic of blended wool—not glossy, not matte. Finely woven with minimal visible pattern. Smooth to the touch. Lining is silk-analog: slippery, cool, with soft luster that contrasts the exterior.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal, navy, or near-black forest green. All are conservative, light-absorbing hues that read as professional in fluorescent corporate offices and dim venue lighting. Deep burgundy silk-analog lining visible only when open—a private luxury detail.
physical_description.closures: Two-button single-breasted closure. Buttons appear to be horn or composite, matte finish to avoid drawing attention.
distinctive_features: Deep, numerous interior pockets—signature Vanthorpe design for carrying credentials, tablets, secure comms
Half-canvassed construction balancing structure with wearing comfort
Burgundy silk-analog lining creates unexpected warmth against the conservative exterior
Notch lapels cut for longevity—neither trendy nor dated
Modest button stance avoids waist emphasis
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional luxury. Accessible to working professionals and aspiring climbers; occasionally purchased by Tier 4 corporate elite as 'casual rotation' piece. Price point Φ420–Φ580.
physical_description.cultural_context: The blazer of choice for mid-level corpo employees, project managers, client-facing roles, and professionals who need to code-switch between formal meetings and working environments. Signals reliability, competence, and respect for professional norms without the stiffness of full formal wear. Worn by those who've accepted corporate hierarchy but haven't yet achieved the wealth to ignore it.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in beautifully. New pieces show crisp structure; worn pieces develop subtle creases at elbows and lapels that enhance rather than diminish appearance. Likely to show minimal wear for years due to quality construction. Occasional dry cleaning maintains shape. Deep pockets show faint interior abrasion from daily use of personal tech.
